title: Jeri
description: Authentic Nepali Jeri is a traditional deep-fried fermented sweet with a distinctive thick flower-shaped pattern, crisp exterior, light chewy interior, and delicate sugar glaze. Commonly enjoyed with fresh buffalo-milk dahi, this classic Nepali mithai is a popular breakfast and festive delicacy throughout Nepal.

ingredients.title: For the Batter
items: Turmeric powder – ½ tsp (or a tiny pinch of orange food color)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Batter
steps: In a large bowl, combine maida, cornflour, rice flour, sugar, salt, and turmeric.
Add yogurt, ghee, and gradually pour in lukewarm water while whisking continuously until smooth.
Beat the batter vigorously for 8–10 minutes until light and lump-free.
Cover and ferment for 12–16 hours at room temperature (26–30°C) until bubbly with a mild fermented aroma.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Preparing the Sugar Syrup
steps: Combine sugar and water in a saucepan and bring to a gentle boil.
Add crushed cardamoms and saffron if using.
Remove from heat and stir in lemon juice and rose water.
Keep the syrup warm (60–70°C) until ready to use.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Finishing the Batter
steps: Just before frying, gently fold baking powder, baking soda, and lemon juice into the fermented batter.
Mix only until combined. The batter should be thick yet pipe smoothly.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Shaping & Frying
steps: Heat ghee or the ghee-oil mixture to 165–170°C.
Transfer the batter into a cloth piping bag with an 8–10 mm opening.
Pipe one thick outer circle, decorative flower-like loops around the edge, one bold inner ring, and a few center loops to create the traditional Nepali Jeri pattern.
Fry slowly for 6–8 minutes, turning once, until deep amber-golden, crisp, and fully cooked.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Syrup Coating
steps: Transfer the hot jeri immediately into the warm sugar syrup.
Soak for only 20–30 seconds, turning once for even coating.
Remove and drain on a wire rack until lightly glazed.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve warm with thick buffalo-milk dahi (traditional Jeri-Dahi).
Pair with freshly brewed Nepali milk tea (Chiya).
Best enjoyed fresh while the exterior remains crisp.
Ideal for breakfast, festivals, and special occasions.

chefTips: Natural fermentation develops the authentic flavor and airy interior.
Use a thick batter and a large piping opening (8–10 mm) to achieve the traditional flower-shaped Nepali jeri.
Maintain frying temperature between 165–170°C for an evenly cooked, crisp texture.
Do not over-soak in syrup—20–30 seconds is enough for a light glossy coating.
One-thread sugar syrup produces the perfect balance of sweetness without making the jeri soggy.
Allow the jeri to rest for 2–3 minutes after draining so the syrup sets into a delicate glaze.
